summary:
Kaduna State stands under Nigeria's national framework, and adds two criminal layers of its own on top of it. The UK Home Office country note (June 2025) records that Kaduna separately adopted a secular Penal Code in 2017 whose Section 259 punishes 'unnatural offences' — sodomy, lesbianism and bestiality — with up to 21 years' imprisonment and a fine, a ceiling above the federal 14-year maximum. Alongside that secular statute runs a parallel Sharia layer applying to Muslims: Kaduna's Sharia Penal Code Law 2002 (Law No. 4 of 2002), signed and brought into operation on 21 June 2002 and gazetted on 4 July 2002.

The penalties in Kaduna's own enacted texts are severe. Ostien's annotated volume records that Kaduna is one of only three states whose statutory wording states that whoever commits sodomy shall be punished with stoning to death (rajm), with no graduation between married and unmarried offenders; the lesbianism offence is left to ta'azir, discretionary punishment by the court. The Home Office's twelve-state Sharia penalties table (section 8.4.3, ILGA-derived) carries Kaduna's row with death by stoning as the maximum for liwat (sodomy) and same-sex acts between women punishable 'at the discretion of the qadi'.

Kaduna is one of the twelve northern states where Sharia courts hold jurisdiction to try criminal cases. Human Rights Watch (2004) traces this to Zamfara's governor introducing the Sharia Establishment Law on 27 October 1999, in force 27 January 2000, with twelve northern states having adopted some form of Sharia into their criminal legislation by 2002; Kaduna remains among them. The practical consequence for a trans visitor in Kaduna is exposure to two concurrent criminal regimes, one secular and one religious, with the religious layer carrying a capital ceiling for men's same-sex acts.
tangentialFactors:
The twelve-state Sharia bloc sets the regional pattern Kaduna belongs to, and Kaduna's own texts sit at its harsher end: its enacted sodomy provision is one of only three state laws specifying stoning to death outright, without the married/unmarried graduation found elsewhere in the bloc.

The 2017 Kaduna Penal Code's 21-year ceiling for 'unnatural offences' exceeds the federal SSMPA maximum of 14 years, so the state layer, not the national statute, sets the operative maximum for a secular conviction in Kaduna.
localsOnly:
Kaduna residents face a two-layer criminal regime: the state's own 2017 secular Penal Code (Section 259, up to 21 years plus fine) and, for Muslims, the parallel Sharia Penal Code Law 2002, whose enacted text specifies stoning to death for sodomy and leaves lesbianism to the qadi's discretion.

Sharia courts in Kaduna have jurisdiction to try criminal cases, a status shared with eleven other northern states and traceable to the wave of Sharia adoption that began with Zamfara's 1999/2000 legislation and was complete across the twelve states by 2002.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not document any Kaduna-specific enforcement incident — no arrests, prosecutions, or violence cases within Kaduna State itself — so the enforcement picture here is drawn from the statutory texts and the Home Office table rather than from state-level case reporting.

No Kaduna-specific data on document markers, facilities access, or care access for trans residents appears in the inventory; those layers are carried by the national record.
